elements.label: section_header
elements.text: TRANSACTION SUMMARY AND COLLATERAL OVERVIEW

elements.label: text
elements.text: Important: This is a fictional synthetic transaction document created solely for demonstrating and evaluating an information-retrieval system. All names, dates, amounts, ratings and transaction terms are invented.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Document purpose

elements.label: text
elements.text: This document presents a consolidated description of the transaction and its collateral management framework. It is designed to contain the types of structured and narrative information that an investor, trustee, analyst or portfolio professional may need to retrieve from a CLO transaction document.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Synthetic transaction document — fictional data for RAG evaluation only.**

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Executive Summary

elements.label: text
elements.text: This document provides a consolidated description of the fictional Northstar CLO 2026-1 transaction, including its capital structure, collateral portfolio, eligibility requirements, concentration limits, coverage tests, payment waterfalls, reinvestment provisions and administrative framework. It is intended to provide a realistic but self-contained information source for retrieval and question-answering evaluation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The transaction combines a diversified portfolio of corporate loan obligations with multiple classes of notes having different levels of seniority and credit protection. The collateral manager has discretion to trade and reinvest within defined limits, while the trustee and other service providers administer the transaction and calculate or report specified transaction information.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Document style: transaction memorandum. This document is intentionally written in a structured memorandum with concise narrative and summary tables.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 1. Transaction Summary

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Transaction identity

elements.label: text
elements.text: Northstar CLO 2026-1 (the **Transaction**) is a fictional collateralized loan obligation transaction designed to acquire and manage a diversified portfolio of primarily senior secured corporate loans. The issuer is **Northstar CLO 2026-1, Ltd.** and the co-issuer is **Northstar CLO 2026-1, LLC**. The transaction closes on **March 18, 2026**, with an effective date of **April 7, 2026**.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The initial target collateral balance is approximately **$465,000,000**. The transaction is denominated in U.S. dollars. The stated legal final maturity is **April 2040**. The non-call period is **12 months** and the reinvestment period is **30 months** from the effective date, subject to the eligibility, concentration and coverage requirements described below.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Key transaction terms

elements.label: text
elements.text: The transaction is intended to generate cash flows from a diversified pool of corporate loan obligations. Cash collections are allocated according to the applicable interest and principal waterfalls, while the collateral manager retains limited trading and reinvestment discretion during the reinvestment period.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 2. Key Parties and Service Providers

elements.label: text
elements.text: The issuer and co-issuer are special-purpose entities established for the transaction. **Apex Meridian Asset Management** serves as collateral manager and is responsible for portfolio selection, monitoring, trading and reinvestment within the transaction restrictions. **JPMorgan Trust Company, N.A.** acts as trustee and performs the administrative and fiduciary functions specified for the transaction.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: **JPMorgan CLO Administration Services** provides collateral administration and reporting services.

elements.label: list_item
elements.text: **Barclays Capital Inc.** acts as placement agent / arranger. The transaction is intended to be rated by

elements.label: footnote
elements.text: **Moody's Ratings and Fitch Ratings**. Calculation, paying-agent, custody and legal functions are performed by the designated transaction service providers under their respective agreements.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Responsibilities

elements.label: text
elements.text: The collateral manager monitors collateral eligibility, concentration compliance and portfolio quality. The trustee maintains transaction accounts and performs payment administration. The collateral administrator receives and processes collateral-level information and supports investor reporting. The calculation agent determines applicable transaction tests and payment calculations according to the governing documents.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 3. Notes and Capital Structure

elements.label: text
elements.text: The notes are divided into senior, mezzanine, junior and subordinated interests. The following table is a fictional transaction summary; exact note balances and terms are subject to the governing transaction documents.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The senior classes are expected to receive priority in the distribution of interest proceeds and principal proceeds. Subordinated interests bear greater loss exposure and receive residual cash flows after satisfaction of the applicable senior obligations.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 4. Interest, Principal and Payment Terms

elements.label: text
elements.text: The rated notes bear interest primarily by reference to a compounded or term SOFR benchmark plus a class-specific spread. Interest is calculated for each quarterly payment period using the applicable day-count convention specified in the transaction documents. Principal is not generally amortized on a fixed schedule during the reinvestment period; principal collections may instead be reinvested when the applicable conditions are satisfied.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Following the reinvestment period, principal proceeds are generally directed toward repayment of the notes in accordance with the principal waterfall. Certain provisions permit refinancing, repricing, reset or optional redemption subject to transaction-specific conditions.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 5. Collateral Portfolio

elements.label: text
elements.text: The collateral portfolio is expected to change over time as borrowers repay loans, assets are sold, new assets are acquired and existing positions are amended. Portfolio statistics therefore represent a point-in-time view rather than a permanent description of the collateral pool.

elements.label: text
elements.text: In addition to the headline portfolio measures, the manager monitors borrower fundamentals, industry exposure, liquidity, loan spread, maturity profile and the potential effect of individual trades on transaction tests. A proposed acquisition can be eligible as an asset but still be unsuitable if it causes a concentration or quality limit to be exceeded. Characteristics

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Portfolio composition

elements.label: text
elements.text: At closing, the portfolio is expected to contain approximately **184 obligors** across a diversified set of industries. The portfolio has an initial collateral balance of approximately **$465,000,000**. The weighted average spread is approximately **3.72%**, and the weighted average life is approximately **5.1 years**.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The portfolio is predominantly composed of senior secured, floating-rate corporate loans. The manager may acquire, dispose of or substitute assets when permitted by the eligibility criteria and concentration limitations.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: Industry and geographic profile

elements.label: text
elements.text: The largest modeled industry exposure at closing is **Software & Services**, subject to a concentration limit of approximately **15.0%**. The remaining portfolio is diversified across multiple industries, including manufacturing, business services, healthcare, software, telecommunications, consumer products and transportation.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The portfolio is primarily U.S.-dollar denominated and focused on North American corporate borrowers. Geographic concentration limits apply to prevent excessive exposure to any single jurisdiction.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 6. Eligibility and Permitted Assets

elements.label: text
elements.text: Eligible collateral generally consists of corporate loan obligations that satisfy the transaction's asset eligibility requirements. Eligible assets are expected to be senior secured or otherwise permitted investments with appropriate maturity, liquidity, currency and credit characteristics.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The manager is required to observe restrictions relating to maximum maturity, minimum spread, permitted currencies, asset type, rating, pricing and default status. Defaulted obligations, discounted obligations and other special assets may be subject to separate limits and haircut or valuation provisions.

elements.label: text
elements.text: A permitted asset generally must have a maturity that does not extend beyond the transaction's legal maturity and must satisfy the applicable concentration and collateral-quality tests at the time of acquisition.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 7. Portfolio Concentration Limits

elements.label: text
elements.text: The portfolio is subject to diversification limits designed to reduce single-obligor, industry, asset-type and rating concentration. A single obligor is generally limited to approximately **2.0%** of the collateral balance. The largest modeled industry concentration is **15.0%**.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Additional limitations apply to second-lien loans, unsecured obligations, fixed-rate assets, CCC or lower-rated obligations, long-dated assets, delayed-draw obligations and other special categories. A breach may restrict purchases or sales until the relevant test is cured.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 8. Collateral Quality and Portfolio Tests

elements.label: text
elements.text: Portfolio quality is monitored using measures including weighted average spread, weighted average life, diversity, rating-related measures and low-rated asset concentration. The target weighted average spread at closing is approximately **3.72%** and the modeled weighted average life is **5.1 years**.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The transaction also monitors recovery assumptions and the composition of assets by seniority, rating and industry. The collateral manager must consider the effect of proposed trades on the applicable collateral-quality tests before executing a transaction.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 9. OC and Interest Coverage Tests

elements.label: text
elements.text: The transaction uses overcollateralization (**OC**) and interest coverage (**IC**) tests to protect senior noteholders.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The tests are measured on specified calculation dates. If a required coverage test is not satisfied, cash that would otherwise flow to junior classes may be redirected to pay senior obligations or build collateral enhancement until the relevant test is cured.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 10. Interest Diversion Mechanism

elements.label: text
elements.text: An interest diversion mechanism may apply when the transaction satisfies specified collateral-quality conditions but requires additional protection for senior classes. Excess interest proceeds can be diverted toward principal or collateral enhancement rather than distributed to subordinated interests.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The calculation agent determines the applicable test using the collateral balance, eligible collateral, required thresholds and other transaction variables. The manager may be restricted from making discretionary distributions while a required condition remains unsatisfied.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 11. Priority of Interest Proceeds

elements.label: text
elements.text: Interest proceeds are applied in a defined order of priority. Subject to the governing documents, the sequence generally begins with taxes and senior administrative expenses, followed by trustee and agency expenses, management-related amounts, senior note interest and then junior note interest.

elements.label: text
elements.text: If coverage or diversion tests are failing, the waterfall may redirect otherwise available cash away from junior distributions. Residual interest proceeds are distributed to subordinated interests only after the required senior obligations and applicable reserves have been satisfied.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 12. Priority of Principal Proceeds

elements.label: text
elements.text: Principal proceeds collected from loan repayments, asset sales and other principal sources are available for reinvestment during the reinvestment period if the transaction conditions permit. Following the reinvestment period, principal proceeds are generally applied sequentially to the rated notes according to their priority.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The principal waterfall may change following an event of default, an optional redemption, a refinancing or another specified transaction event. Equity and subordinated interests receive residual principal only after higher-ranking obligations have been satisfied.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 13. Reinvestment and Trading Provisions

elements.label: text
elements.text: The reinvestment period is **30 months**. During this period, the manager may use principal proceeds to acquire eligible collateral, subject to the portfolio eligibility criteria, concentration limits, collateral-quality tests and coverage tests.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The manager may also sell or substitute assets when permitted. Trading decisions must consider the effect of the proposed transaction on weighted average spread, weighted average life, rating metrics, diversity, concentration limits and coverage tests.

elements.label: text
elements.text: After the reinvestment period terminates, principal proceeds are generally directed toward deleveraging rather than ordinary reinvestment, subject to limited permitted trading and substitution provisions.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 14. Optional Redemption, Refinancing and Reset

elements.label: text
elements.text: The transaction includes a non-call period of **12 months**. Following the applicable non-call period, the notes may be subject to optional redemption, refinancing, repricing or reset if the required conditions and voting thresholds are satisfied.

elements.label: text
elements.text: A clean-up call may also be available when the outstanding collateral balance falls below a specified percentage of its original balance. Redemption proceeds are allocated according to the applicable priority of payments.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 15. Fees, Expenses and Administrative Costs

elements.label: text
elements.text: Transaction expenses include management fees, trustee and administrative fees, collateral administration fees, rating expenses, legal expenses and other costs associated with maintaining the transaction.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The collateral manager receives a management fee subject to the applicable waterfall and fee cap. Senior transaction expenses generally receive priority over junior distributions.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 16. Collateral Manager Authority and Restrictions

elements.label: text
elements.text: The collateral manager has authority to select, acquire, sell and reinvest collateral within the permitted investment guidelines. The manager must observe eligibility, concentration, collateral-quality and coverage requirements.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Manager powers are constrained by prohibited-investment rules, conflicts provisions, trading restrictions, valuation requirements and transaction tests. Replacement or termination of the manager may occur following specified events and voting procedures.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 17. Events of Default and Enforcement

elements.label: text
elements.text: Events of default may include failure to make required payments, specified breaches of transaction documents, insolvency-related events and other defined defaults. Following an event of default, the trustee and eligible noteholders may exercise specified remedies.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Remedies can include acceleration, enforcement against transaction assets and application of proceeds under a post-default waterfall. The rights of each note class remain subject to the priority and voting provisions of the transaction documents.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 18. Voting, Consent and Amendment Matters

elements.label: text
elements.text: Certain amendments require approval from holders of specified classes or percentages of outstanding notes. Extraordinary matters may require higher consent thresholds than routine administrative amendments.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Class voting rights are generally designed to protect the economic interests of each tranche. Subordinated interests may have separate rights on manager replacement, redemption, refinancing or other matters where permitted.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 19. Reporting, Calculation and Administration

elements.label: text
elements.text: The trustee and collateral administrator prepare or distribute periodic reports containing collateral balances, transaction tests, note balances, payments and other investor information.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Reports may include monthly collateral information, quarterly payment-date calculations, coverage-test results, portfolio statistics and transaction-level compliance information. The calculation agent is responsible for determining specified tests and payment amounts under the governing documents.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 20. Key Transaction Risks

elements.label: text
elements.text: Investors are exposed to credit losses, defaults, recoveries below expectations, interest-rate movements, reinvestment risk, liquidity risk, concentration risk and counterparty risk. The value and cash flow of the notes depend on the performance of the underlying collateral.

elements.label: text
elements.text: Additional risks arise from manager discretion, structural subordination, coverage-test breaches, refinancing conditions, changes in market liquidity, changes in law or regulation and potential conflicts among different classes of investors.

elements.label: text
elements.text: The subordinated and equity interests generally bear losses before senior noteholders and may receive no distributions in periods of weak collateral performance.

elements.label: section_header
elements.text: 21. Selected Definitions

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Overcollateralization (OC):** A ratio comparing the collateral value or adjusted collateral balance with the principal amount of specified classes of notes.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Interest Coverage (IC):** A ratio comparing available interest proceeds with the interest obligations of specified note classes.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Reinvestment Period:** The period during which principal proceeds may generally be reinvested in eligible collateral, subject to transaction conditions.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Non-Call Period:** The initial period during which specified optional redemption rights are restricted.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Interest Proceeds:** Cash flows attributable to interest and other income from the collateral.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Principal Proceeds:** Cash flows attributable to principal repayment, sales and other principal sources.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Defaulted Obligation:** A collateral obligation meeting the transaction's contractual definition of default.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Weighted Average Spread:** A portfolio-level measure of the weighted average spread earned by the collateral.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Weighted Average Life:** A weighted estimate of the remaining principal repayment timing of portfolio assets.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Diversity Score:** A measure used to evaluate portfolio diversification across obligors and industries.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Collateral Principal Balance:** The amount of collateral principal recognized for transaction calculations after applying applicable adjustments.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Interest Diversion Test:** A transaction test that may redirect interest proceeds toward principal or senior protection when specified conditions apply.

elements.label: text
elements.text: **Synthetic-data notice:** All transaction names, parties, financial amounts, ratings, dates, portfolio statistics and contractual provisions in this document are fictional and are provided solely for testing and demonstrating an information-retrieval system.
